name: Helix Corp Administrative Dress Shirt
description:
The standard-issue dress shirt for Helix Corporation's administrative and client-facing staff, distributed through internal requisition rather than purchased. A slim-fit, spread-collar design in pale steel blue — a color Helix has trademarked internally as 'Helix Meridian Blue' — with subtle vertical texture woven into the fabric. The Helix helix logo appears on the left chest in a tone-on-tone embroidery that's only visible at certain angles. Buttons are small and matte, matched exactly to the fabric color.

The shirt is well-constructed and comfortable enough for twelve-hour office shifts, which is intentional — Helix wants its staff presentable and not distracted by discomfort. Wearing this outside of work hours is technically permitted but subtly discouraged by HR guidance. Plenty of Helix employees wear it anyway, because it's the nicest shirt they own.
what_it_says: You work for Helix, or you want people to think you do, or you're trying to get into a Helix facility.
worn_by: corponation employees across various firms who received it as a gift
story_hooks: A Helix shirt has appeared in a Tier 1 second-hand stall — still pressed, still tagged. How did it get there, and who was wearing it last?
Helix has quietly embedded a micro-woven identifier thread in its current batch of shirts — a passive RFID-analog that logs building entry. Most employees don't know.
A character is trying to bluff their way into a Helix facility and needs the shirt, the badge, and the right way to walk. They have two of the three.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, corporate-coded dress shirt that reads as upper-tier professional. The pale steel blue creates a cool, clinical impression—corporate but approachable. The slim fit skims the body without clinging, projecting understated confidence and desk-work competence. On the street, it signals either a Helix employee or someone aspirational enough to own one.
physical_description.fit: Slim, tailored through the shoulders and torso with a slight taper at the waist. Designed for prolonged seated wear—ergonomic rather than fashion-forward. Sleeves hit just at the wrist bone. Not restrictive; built for comfort during marathon office shifts.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grade synthetic blend—likely 60% recycled polyester, 40% lab-grown cotton analog. Smooth finish with subtle moisture-wicking properties. Durable enough to survive corporate laundry cycles and cheap enough to replace if lost in a Helix relocation.
physical_description.texture: Deceptively textured: the fabric has a fine vertical weave that catches light subtly, preventing the shirt from looking flat or cheap. Up close, the weave is visible but not rough. The buttons are matte, slightly textured to prevent glare under office lighting.
physical_description.color_scheme: Proprietary 'Helix Meridian Blue'—a pale, cool steel blue that sits between industrial gray and soft cyan. The tone-on-tone helix logo on the left chest is embroidered in a fractionally darker blue, visible only when light hits it directly. White or silver thread would break the brand cohesion, so Helix chose subtlety.
physical_description.closures: Standard matte buttons, small and precisely matched to the shirt fabric. Six buttons down the front; one at each cuff. No visible branding on buttons themselves—Helix reserves overt logos for less visible placements.
distinctive_features: Tone-on-tone embroidered helix logo on left chest—visible only at certain angles, a subtle corporate flex
Fine vertical texture woven throughout, preventing a flat corporate appearance
Spread collar designed to sit well under a Helix-issued blazer or on its own
Invisible internal reinforcement at stress points (button holes, collar, cuffs)—built to last
Micro-perforations in fabric blend allow airflow during long office days
Seams are precisely finished; no loose threads even when new
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2 corporate issue. Not luxury, but solidly above working-class. Free distribution signals employee value without actual wage increases.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this outside work hours reads as either: (a) loyal Helix employee, (b) someone who can't afford better, or (c) someone performing corporate competence. On the street, it marks you as office-bound, potentially middle-management or administrative. In a Tier 5 zone, it might make you a target.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when issued, quickly becoming 'broken-in' within a week. After a few months: slightly softer, faint creasing at the elbows and chest from wear, but still presentable. Helix employees often wear these outside the office because they're the nicest thing they own; street wear shows more visible wrinkles and minor stains.

image_prompt: Neo-noir fashion photography: a slim administrative worker in a pale steel blue Helix Corp dress shirt, shot from the waist up against a dark urban backdrop. Moody cyan and blue lighting emphasizes the subtle vertical texture of the fabric and catches the tone-on-tone helix logo embroidered on the left chest, making it flicker in and out of visibility. The spread collar sits crisp and clinical. Background: rain-slicked mega-building facade, holographic Helix signage blurred behind. Model has mixed heritage features, subtle augmentation visible at the temple. Shirt is pristine, recently laundered. Midjourney style: corporate glamour meets street authenticity. --ar 2:3 --v 6
